data.narrative:
Chariot Defense is a Series A defense & security company that has raised $41M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a peer set of 11 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies comprising 2 public comparables (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms including Anduril Industries, Helsing, and Singularity.

Two methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $41M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier for Series A advancement, yielding $82M. Peer-median analysis examines the 11-company Defense & Security cohort, which spans $125M to $3.0B (Dream Security at the high end, Code Metal, Twenty, Harmattan AI, and Allen Control Systems in the $1.2B–$2.2B band). The median valuation across this peer set is $1.0B.

The triangulated range is $70M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $541M. The substantial spread reflects meaningful heterogeneity in the peer universe and stage variation within the comparable set. Key uncertainties include revenue scale and customer diversification relative to the median peer, product maturity relative to Series B-stage comparables, and capital efficiency relative to the $41M already deployed. The wide range underscores that stage-progression and peer-median methods yield materially different implications; specificity on Chariot's revenue, margins, and customer concentration would narrow this band considerably.
